item.title: A new mayor, but a familiar face
item.description: Weiser’s City Council voted unanimously to appoint Council President Herb Haun as mayor following Randy Hibberd’s health‑related resignation. Haun, pictured left was elected in 2023, and has filled in several times during Hibberd’s recent absences. Seated next to Haun is Councilor Lisa Horzen, who was elected in 2025. item.title: County finances stable, reserves strong
item.description: Washington County received a positive financial review during its annual audit presentation on Feb. 2. Independent auditor Kurt Folke of Quest CPAs reported that the county ended the 2025 fiscal year in a strong position and with healthy reserves across all major funds. Folke briefed the Board of County Commissioners on the results of the audit, which included three required reports: the financial statement audit, the internal controls and compliance review, and the federal single audit report.

item.title: Judge dismisses claims against former officials
item.description: A settlement agreement between the county and the plaintiffs in a lawsuit includes the county rerouting Gentry Lane within 12 months. Photo by Nancy Grindstaff Third District Judge Davis VanderVelde has dismissed all remaining claims against former Washington County prosecutor Delton Walker and former county commissioner Lyndon Haines, effectively ending the litigation against both men in a long running dispute over land use decisions and access along Gentry Lane.
